run.subject: Let the harness drive a build that predates one of its instruments

gm1-bml-fat.note: priority bitmap layer, transparent and fat pixels

gm1-bml-full.note: full-width opaque priority bitmap - the tile pass is skipped

gm1-bml-pri.note: priority bitmap layer - over layer 1, under layer 2, under sprites

gm1-coarse.note: coarse scroll to cell 20, single name page

gm1-coarse-hpage.note: coarse scroll past the end with the horizontal page swap on

gm1-ecm0.note: one tile layer, the ECM0 emitter

gm1-hscroll-7.note: layer 1 fine scroll 7 - a whole cell bar one pixel

gm1-hscroll-split.note: layers scrolled by different amounts - tmsCopyAlignMask

gm1-layers-off.note: both tile layers disabled - only the backdrop may remain

gm1-locked.note: plain TMS9918 Graphics I - renderTileRowLocked, no F18A anything

gm1-palette.note: palette select for layer 1, layer 2 and sprites at once

gm1-posattr.note: attributes by position rather than by name, ECM1

gm1-posattr-pages.note: position attributes read from a name table whose base already carries the page bits. They are added to the colour table base, so the attributes are 0xC00 along from it - and a differently coloured table sits where forcing the bits instead of adding them would read. Real software puts its name table there; nothing else here does

gm1-priority.note: ECM2 priority tiles over sprites - attribute bit 7

gm1-priority-scroll.note: priority tiles over sprites with both layers finely scrolled by different amounts. A scrolled row starts its first tile left of the screen, and the sprite mask a priority tile clears is in screen pixels - so that tile is the one case the two disagree on

gm1-scroll-both.note: both layers scrolled in both axes, all four registers different - the case where a scroll taken from the wrong layer or the wrong axis has nowhere to hide

gm1-scroll-cross.note: layer 1 across, layer 2 down - the two layers on different axes, which no scene reached and one real dump does

gm1-scroll-cross-back.note: layer 1 down, layer 2 across - the other way round, because the two layers take their scroll from different registers and a shared address generator

gm1-sprites.note: sprites over both tile layers, ECM0

gm1-sprites-ecm1.note: 32 ECM1 sprites, one bit plane - the emitter's cheapest index

gm1-sprites-ecm3.note: 32 ECM3 sprites, three bit planes - 2048 quads a frame, which is the densest the 32-sprite limit allows

gm1-sprites-ecm3-mag.note: 16 magnified ECM3 sprites, which is the other ECM emit loop: four pixels into an aligned buffer, then doubled out under the collision mask. Sixteen because a magnified sprite covers 32 scanlines, so this is the same 2048 quads - and 32 of them do not fit at 252 MHz

gm1-t1-off.note: layer 1 disabled with layer 2 on - D4's second case

gm1-t2-ecm0.note: both tile layers, ECM0 - the selection mask and the composite

gm1-t2-hscroll.note: layer 2 scrolled across and layer 1 not - the only arrangement where the second layer's own scroll is what places it, with nothing on the first to move with it

gm1-t2-vscroll.note: layer 2 scrolled down and layer 1 not

gm1-t2-vscroll-page.note: both layers scrolled vertically into their other pages

gm1-vscroll.note: layer 1 vertical scroll 100, no page swap

gm1-vscroll-page.note: vertical scroll wrapping into the other name page

gm2.note: Graphics II, three pattern and colour pages, full name mask

gm2-bml-pri.note: a priority bitmap layer in Graphics II - under the tiles it outranks, over layer 1, under sprites

gm2-ecm3.note: Graphics II at ECM3 - ECM composes with the mode through the plane 1 address alone, so the thirds become per-third colour sets (plan 2.8)

gm2-locked.note: Graphics II locked - same path, no F18A palette

gm2-namemask.note: R3 low bits masking the name to 0-63, colour page fixed

gm2-nosplit.note: R4 page bits clear, so all three thirds read page 0

gm2-palette.note: R0x18 palette select, which GM2 applies to non-zero colours only

gm2-posattr.note: position attributes have no effect in an ECM0 graphics mode: they move the attribute address, which only ECM1-3 reads

gm2-scroll.note: Graphics II with both scrolls - the pattern third follows the scrolled row

gm2-t2.note: Graphics II with tile layer 2 - both layers share the colour table, because the GM2 colour base is a single register bit

mcm.note: Multicolor - the pattern byte is the colour pair

mcm-bml-pri.note: Multicolor with a priority bitmap layer

mcm-ecm3.note: Multicolor at ECM3, which is not multicolour at all: the faked pattern is ECM0-only, so only the plane 1 address survives (plan 2.8)

mcm-scroll.note: Multicolor with both scrolls - the vertical one moves which tiles are fetched but not which four-line block of each is shown (plan 2.5)

t40.note: 40-column text, six pixels a cell, one colour pair

t40-48rows.note: 40 columns by 48 rows - R0 bit 3 renders every VGA line instead of doubling it, so the same 24 rows of cells become 48 and the renderer has half a line's time to make each one

t40-48rows-sprites.note: sprites over 48-row text. The sprite grid does not double with the rows - the library halves y before it plans a sprite - so each sprite covers two rendered lines and its own y is still 0-191. What the sprites add is what the diagnostic overlay then pushes over

t40-60rows.note: 40 columns by 60 rows - 30 rows doubled, 480 rendered lines, the tallest frame this firmware produces. Its worst row clears a 31.8 us line by under a microsecond, so the six-pixel cell being the expensive text emitter still shows here more than anywhere: the diagnostic overlay puts it back over

t40-bml-pri.note: a priority bitmap layer in 40-column text, arbitrated by the same composite the graphics modes use

t40-bml-under.note: a bitmap layer below 40-column text, with the first three cells of every row at colour zero. A cell whose colour byte is zero draws no pixel at all at all, so the layer under it must show - and a *leading* run of them is the one place that used to paint the backdrop instead (D8)

t40-ecm1.note: 40-column text at ECM1: two bitplanes, and the sub-palette from the attribute byte instead of a colour pair. The attribute is indexed by name, which is the form position attributes are off

t40-ecm3.note: 40-column text at ECM3 - four bitplanes, and the bottom band's punctuation carries every combination of priority, flipX, flipY and transparent

t40-ecm3-posattr.note: ECM3 text with position attributes, so the attribute walks with the cell and its address takes the row offset that a by-name one must not

t40-ecm3-scroll.note: ECM3 text scrolled both ways: the row runs two cells long and the priority clear has to reach the sprite mask in screen pixels, not buffer ones

t40-ecm3-sprites.note: sprites under ECM3 text, where the attribute's priority bit decides per cell which is on top

t40-hscroll-past-row.note: text scrolled further than a row is wide, which the F18A does not wrap. Its column counter is seeded with hscroll/6 and wraps on reaching the last column, so a start cell of 40 never meets 39 and the row reads on into the next one: the layer comes out a character row high. Layer 1 at 240 lands on the boundary exactly, layer 2 at 250 a row and four pixels past it

t40-hscroll-split.note: both text layers scrolled horizontally by different amounts - tmsCopyAlignMask over a six-pixel cell

t40-locked.note: 40-column text locked - no sprites at all

t40-palette.note: both 40-column text layers on their own sub-palettes. Text takes the tile palette select like every other mode: an ECM0 pixel is PIX, PRI, then `tileps_s & pix_colr_s`, and the backdrop is built the same way from layer 1's selector

t40-posattr.note: 40-column text with a colour byte per cell - the 6-pixel 8bpp emitter

t40-scroll.note: 40-column text with both scroll registers set. 163 pixels is cell 27 plus one, so the row wraps to its own first cell partway across

t40-scroll-cross.note: 40-column text with layer 1 across and layer 2 down - the six-pixel cell has its own scroll arithmetic and its own emitter

t40-sprites.note: sprites over 40-column text, which only the F18A allows

t40-t2.note: both 40-column text layers, layer 2 blended in as it is emitted - the same shape 80 columns uses, and for the same reason

t40-t2-ecm3.note: both 40-column text layers at ECM3 - the coverage mask six pixels at a time, from the plane mask rather than the colour byte

t80-48rows.note: 80 columns by 48 rows - 3840 cells, twice the rows at the narrowest cell

t80-60rows.note: 80 columns by 60 rows - 4800 cells over 480 rendered lines, which is every pixel this board can address and the heaviest frame in the library. Its colour table does not fit under NAME2, so it takes that space

t80-bml-pri.note: 80-column text with a priority bitmap layer

t80-hscroll.note: both 80-column layers scrolled horizontally by different amounts. The offset inside the first cell is only ever 0, 2 or 4 pixels (plan 2.4), so the emitter backs up whole cells and keeps its three-word store

t80-hscroll-past-row.note: the same overrun at 80 columns, and at the same register value. Worth its own scene because it is not the same code: without the 8bpp tier a TEXT80 line falls past the branch the 40-column one takes and is emitted packed two pixels to a byte, so a change to either emitter moves one of these two and not the other

t80-hscroll-plain.note: 80-column text scrolled with the two colours from R7 - three byte stores a cell, so the wrap is a second run rather than a test

t80-posattr.note: 80-column text with a colour byte per cell

t80-scroll-cross.note: 80-column text with layer 1 across and layer 2 down

t80-sprites.note: sprites over 80-column text, on their own 256-pixel grid

t80-t2.note: both text layers, layer 2 blended inside the layer 2 pass

t80-t2-sparse.note: layer 2 mostly empty, so the four-cell transparent skip fires

t80-vscroll.note: both text layers scrolled vertically by different amounts

t80-vscroll-page.note: 80-column text scrolling past its last row with the vertical page size bit set, which does nothing: a text row's name address is a row count times a column count and the page bit is never part of it in either direction
